meta.title: Directive 2012/13/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 22 May 2012 on the right to information in criminal proceedings

items.text: This Directive lays down rules concerning the right to information of suspects or accused persons, relating to their rights in criminal proceedings and to the accusation against them. It also lays down rules concerning the right to information of persons subject to a European Arrest Warrant relating to their rights.
items.heading: Article 1
items.comment: Implicitly transposed by the Italian Legislative Decree n. 101/2014. For reference to the EAW see Article 5 of this Directive

items.heading: Article 2

items.text: 1. This Directive applies from the time persons are made aware by the competent authorities of a Member State that they are suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence until the conclusion of the proceedings, which is understood to mean the final determination of the question whether the suspect or accused person has committed the criminal offence, including, where applicable, sentencing and the resolution of any appeal.
items.comment: The Directive in Italy applies only to criminal proceedings.

items.text: 2. Where the law of a Member State provides for the imposition of a sanction regarding minor offences by an authority other than a court having jurisdiction in criminal matters, and the imposition of such a sanction may be appealed to such a court, this Directive shall apply only to the proceedings before that court, following such an appeal.
items.comment: No such procedure exists under Italian law.

items.heading: Article 3
items.comment: Article 3 of the Directive is implemented in a number of different provisions of the Italian Criminal Procedure Code, which are detailed below.

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons are provided promptly with information concerning at least the following procedural rights, as they apply under national law, in order to allow for those rights to be exercised effectively:

(a)

the right of access to a lawyer;

provisions.comment:
Pre-trial investigation.

Acts carried out by the Prosecutor, to which the lawyer has the right to be present. According to the Supreme Court's case-law, such notice is given at the moment/straight after the carry out of the activity in which the lawyer has the right to be present if the activity requires a "surprise effect" (e.g. search and seizure). See Cass. Sez. Un. n. 7/2000, Mariano.

The failure to send the notice of investigation is sanctioned by nullity of the investigative act pursuant to art. 178, para, 1, letter. c), of the criminal procedure code. However, this procedural sanction does not occur in the case of sending of documents deemed equivalent by the Court of cassation, such as the summons to appear for questioning (see art. 375 of the criminal procedure code) or the notice of the day, time and place set for the assignment of the non-repeatable technical ascertainment pursuant to art. 360 of the criminal procedure code.
provisions.textEn: 1. Only when the Public Prosecutor must carry out an activity in which the lawyer has the right to be present, shall he/she send a notice of investigation to the suspect and the victim by mail, in a sealed registered envelope with return receipt. The notice of investigation shall contain the legal provisions which have allegedly been violated as well as the date and place in which the criminal act was committed along with a request to exercise the right of appointing a retained lawyer.

provisions.comment: Pre-trial investigation. This information is provided along with the one under Article 369 of the Criminal Procure Code (or, at the latest, with the notice on the conclusion of preliminary investigations according to Article 415-bis), if the suspect does not have a retained lawyer.
provisions.textEn:
1. During the first activity in which the lawyer has the right to be present and, in any case, prior to sending the summons to appear for questioning according to the conjunction of Articles 375, paragraph 3, and 416, or no later than the service of the notice on the conclusion of preliminary investigations according to Article 415-bis, the Public Prosecutor, under penalty of nullity of subsequent acts, shall serve on the suspected person the notification on the designation of a court-appointed lawyer.


2. The notification referred to in paragraph 1 shall contain:

a) the information that technical defence in criminal proceedings is mandatory, along with the specification of the rights assigned by law to the suspected person;

b) the name of the court-appointed lawyer, his/her address and his/her telephone number;

c) the specification of the right to appoint a retained lawyer, along with the notice that, if the suspect does not have a retained lawyer, he/she shall be assisted by the court-appointed lawyer;

d) the specification of the obligation to remunerate the court-appointed lawyer, unless the conditions for accessing the benefit referred to in letter e) are met, along with the warning that, in case the lawyer is not paid, mandatory enforcement shall be imposed;

[...]

provisions.comment: At the time of the enforcement of a precautionary detention order.
provisions.textEn:
Without prejudice to Article 156, the official or officer in charge of enforcing the order of precautionary detention shall provide the accused person with a copy of the decision along with a clear and precise written notice. If the accused does not know the Italian language, the notice shall be translated into a language he/she understands. The notice shall contain the following information:

a) his/her right to appoint a retained lawyer [...]

provisions.comment: At the time of the arrest/temporary detention ("fermo").
provisions.textEn:
The police officials and officers who have arrested or placed under temporary detention ("fermo") the perpetrator or to whom the arrested person has been surrendered, shall immediately inform the Public Prosecutor of the place where the perpetrator has been arrested or placed under temporary detention.

They shall provide the arrested or temporarily detained person ("fermato") with a written notice, drafted clearly and precisely. If the arrested or temporarily detained person does not know the Italian language, the notice shall be translated into a language he understands. The notice shall contain the following information:

a) his/her right to appoint a retained lawyer [...];

provisions.comment:
Pre-trial investigation.

Acts carried out by the police of its own initiative, to which the suspect's lawyer has the right to be present. The suspect, straight before the carry out of these acts, is informed by the police of such right pursuant to art. 114 of the Implementing provisions of the code of criminal procedure (see below).
provisions.textEn: The suspect's lawyer may be present, without having the right to be informed in advance, during the actions provided for in Articles 352 [searches] and 354 [urgent checks of the scene, objects and persons and seizure], as well as at the immediate opening of the envelope, as authorised by the Public Prosecutor under Article 353, paragraph 2.

provisions.comment:
Pre-trial investigation.

When police officials collect on their own initiative summary information from the suspect, the necessary participation of the retained or court-appointed lawyer is required. To this purpose, the police shall warn the suspect of her/his right to be assisted by a lawyer before the start of the questioning.
provisions.textEn:
1. Police officials shall collect, as provided for in Article 64, summary information useful for investigative purposes from the suspect who has not been placed under arrest or temporary detention according to Article 384 and in the cases referred to in Article 384-bis.

2. Prior to the investigative questioning, the criminal police shall require the suspect to appoint a retained lawyer and, if he does not do so, the police shall follow the provisions of Article 97, paragraph 3.

3. Investigative questioning shall be performed with the necessary assistance of the lawyer who shall be promptly informed by the criminal police. The lawyer must be present during investigative questioning.

4. If the lawyer has not been found or he did not appear, the criminal police shall require the Public Prosecutor to take a decision according to Article 97, paragraph 4.

provisions.comment:

provisions.textEn:
1. If the Public Prosecutor must carry out a questioning, inspection, informal identification or line-up in which the suspect must participate, the Public Prosecutor shall require the suspect to appear according to Article 375.

2. The suspected person who does not have a lawyer shall also be informed that he shall be assisted by a court-appointed lawyer, but that he may also appoint a retained lawyer.

provisions.comment:

provisions.textEn: 1. If the Public Prosecutor performs searches or seizures, he shall ask the suspect, when the latter is present, whether he is assisted by a retained lawyer and, if he does not have one, the Public Prosecutor shall appoint a court-appointed lawyer according to Article 97, paragraph 3.

provisions.comment:
Pre-trial investigation.

Non-repeatable technical ascertainments, to which the suspect's lawyer has the right to be present.
provisions.textEn:
1. If the ascertainment provided for in Article 359 involves persons, objects or places which are subject to change, the Public Prosecutor shall inform, without delay, the suspect, the victim and the lawyers of the day, time and place set for the assignment of the non-repeatable technical ascertainment and of the right to appoint technical consultants.

2. The provisions of Article 364, paragraph 2, shall apply.

3. The lawyers as well as the possibly appointed technical consultants have the right to be present during the assignment of the non-repeatable technical ascertainment, participate in the ascertainment and make their own observations and reservations.

items.comment:
Specific framework in this regard is provided only in relation to the information given in case of deprivation of liberty of the suspects or accused persons. Articles 293 and 386 of the Italian Criminal Procedure Code (detailed below) require the information to be written "clearly and precisely". Nevertheless, this does not necessarily guarantee that the meaning of the information provided is accessible to the general public.

No specific provision for vulnerable suspects or accused persons is provided. The Italian legislator has not implemented a specific legal framework concerning the information duties for children, as required by Article 4 of the Directive 2016/800/EU.

items.heading: Article 4
items.comment: The Letter of Rights on arrest is implemented in different provisons of the Italian Criminal Procedure Code relating to both precautionary measures and arrest and temporary detention ("fermo").

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons who are arrested or detained are provided promptly with a written Letter of Rights. They shall be given an opportunity to read the Letter of Rights and shall be allowed to keep it in their possession throughout the time that they are deprived of liberty.

provisions.comment: At the time of the enforcement of a precautionary detention order.
provisions.textEn: Without prejudice to Article 156, the official or officer in charge of enforcing the order of precautionary detention shall provide the accused person with a copy of the decision along with a clear and precise written notice. provisions.comment: Control made by the judge at the questioning of the person subject to a personal precautionary measure.
provisions.textEn:
1. In the stages of the proceedings prior to the opening of the trial, the court that has decided on the application of the precautionary measure shall question the person under precautionary detention in prison immediately and in any case by the fifth day after the enforcement of detention, if it has not done so during the hearing which confirmed the arrest or temporary detention of the crime suspect, except for

the case in which he/she cannot be questioned in any way whatsoever.

1 -bis. If the person is subject to a different precautionary measure, either coercive or disqualifying, the questioning shall take place no later than ten days after enforcement of the decision or its service. The court shall verify, also of its own motion, that the accused person under precautionary detention in prison or house arrest has received the notice referred to in Article 293, paragraph 1, or has been informed according to paragraph 1 -bis of the same Article, and shall give or complete the written notice or the oral information, if necessary.

If the arrested or temporarily detained person does not know the Italian language, the notice shall be translated into a language he/she understands.

provisions.comment: Control made by the judge at the confirmation hearing of the arrest/temporary detention ("fermo").
provisions.textEn:
1. Confirmation hearings are held in closed session with the necessary participation of the lawyer of the arrested or temporarily detained person.

2. If the retained or court-appointed lawyer cannot be reached or has not appeared, the Preliminary Investigation Judge shall decide on the designation of a substitute according to Article 97, paragraph 4.

The Judge shall verify, also of his/her own motion, that the arrested or temporarily detained person ("fermato") has received the notice referred to in Article 386, paragraph 1, or has been informed according to paragraph 1-bis of the same Article, and shall give or complete the written notice or the oral information, if necessary.

items.comment:
Articles 293 and 386 of the Italian Criminal Procedure Code provide that the Letter of Rights shall be given by the police at the moment of the enforcement of the precautionary detention order or of the arrest/temporary detention ("fermo"). No specific sanction is foreseen in case of disregard of such duty (see also below, under Article 8(2)). In that case, the information can still be provided by the competent judge who controls the legality of the deprivation of liberty (see Articles 294-bis and 391, par. 2, below).

The Italian Criminal Procedure Code does not provide any specific provision on the opportunity for the suspects or accused persons to read the Letter of Rights and on the permission to keep it in their possession throughout the time that they are deprived of liberty.

items.heading: Article 5
items.subHeading: Letter of Rights in European Arrest Warrant proceedings
items.comment: The Letter of Rights in European Arrest Warrant proceedings is regulated by the Italian law n. 69/2005 implementing Framework Decision 2002/584/JHA.

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that persons who are arrested for the purpose of the execution of a European Arrest Warrant are provided promptly with an appropriate Letter of Rights containing information on their rights according to the law implementing Framework Decision 2002/584/JHA in the executing Member State.

provisions.textEn:
1. The police official who arrested the individual pursuant to Article 11 shall inform him/her, in a language he understands, of the warrant issued and of its content and provide him/her with a written notice, drafted clearly and precisely, which informs him/her of the possibility of consenting to his/her surrender to the issuing judicial authority and warns him/her of the right to appoint a retained lawyer and to be assisted by an interpreter. If the arrested person fails to appoint a lawyer, the police immediately identifies a court-appointed lawyer pursuant to article 97 of the criminal procedure code.

1-bis. The provision of article 9, paragraph 5-bis, first sentence applies.

2. The judicial police shall promptly inform the lawyer of the arrest.

3. The report of the arrest acknowledges, under penalty of nullity, the fulfilments indicated in paragraphs 1 and 2, as well as checks made on the identification of the arrested person.

[...]

provisions.comment: The information on the right to appoint a lawyer in the issuing State must also be given by the police to the arrested person (see Article 12, par. 1-bis, above). In this case, though, the disregard of such duty is not sanctioned by nullity.
provisions.textEn: When executing the order referred to in paragraph 4, the police official or agent also informs the requested person of the faculty to appoint a lawyer in the issuing State. The President of the Court of Appeal gives immediate notice to the competent authority of the issuing State of such appointment or of the will of the interested person to make use of a lawyer in the issuing State.

items.text: 2. The Letter of Rights shall be drafted in simple and accessible language. An indicative model Letter of Rights is set out in Annex II.

If the arrested person fails to appoint a lawyer, the police immediately identifies a court-appointed lawyer pursuant to article 97 of the criminal procedure code.

items.comment:
Article 12, para. 1, of the Italian Law n. 69/2005 requires the information to be written "clearly and precisely". Nevertheless, this does not necessarily guarantee that the meaning of the information provided is accessible to the general public.

A model Letter of Rights is set out in Annex II.

items.heading: Article 6
items.subHeading: Right to information about the accusation
items.comment: The right to information about the accusation is implemented in a number of provisions of the Italian Criminal Procedure Code, which are detailed below.

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons are provided with information about the criminal act they are suspected or accused of having committed. That information shall be provided promptly and in such detail as is necessary to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings and the effective exercise of the rights of the defence.

provisions.comment:
Pre-trial investigation.

According to the Supreme Court's case-law, such notice is given at the moment/straight after the carry out of the activity in which the lawyer has the right to be present if the activity requires a "surprise effect" (e.g. search and seizure). See Cass. Sez. Un. n. 7/2000, Mariano.

At this stage, the suspect is not informed in detail of the criminal act.

Should the legal definition of the criminal act change during the investigation, the suspect is not provided with a new notice, but, pursuant to Article 369, para. 1-bis, the suspect is made aware of his/her right to have access to the notitiae criminis register, which must be updated by the Public Prosecutor after any change in the definition of the criminal act (see Article 335, para. 2, of the Italian Criminal Procedure Code).
provisions.textEn:
1. Only when the Public Prosecutor must carry out an activity in which the lawyer has the right to be present, shall he/she send a notice of investigation to the suspect and the victim by mail, in a sealed registered envelope with return receipt. The notice of investigation shall contain the legal provisions which have allegedly been violated as well as the date and place in which the criminal act was committed along with a request to exercise the right of appointing a retained lawyer.

1-bis. The Public Prosecutor shall also inform the suspect and the victim of their right to being informed as set forth in Article 335, paragraph 3.

provisions.comment: Pre-trial investigation.
provisions.textEn: With the exception of the crimes referred to in Article 407, paragraph 2, letter a.), the alleged perpetrator of the offence, the victim and the lawyers, upon their own request, shall be informed of the entering of notitiae criminis according to paragraphs 1 and 2.

provisions.comment: At the end of pre-trial investigation.
provisions.textEn:
1. Prior to the expiry of the time limit provided for in paragraph 2 of Article 405, also if extended, when the case must not be discontinued under Articles 408 and 411, the Public Prosecutor shall serve the notice on the conclusion of preliminary investigations on the suspect and his/her lawyer. When any of the offences referred to in Articles 572 and 612-bis of the Criminal Code are prosecuted, the same notice shall be served on the victim's lawyer or, in his/her absence, the victim himself.

2. The notice shall contain a brief description of the criminal act under prosecution, the rules of law allegedly violated, the date and place of the act, along with the notice that the record of the completed investigations is filed with the Clerk‟s Office of the Public Prosecutor and the suspect and his/her lawyer shall be entitled to examine it and copy it.

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons who are arrested or detained are informed of the reasons for their arrest or detention, including the criminal act they are suspected or accused of having committed.

provisions.comment: At the time of the enforcement of a precautionary detention order.
provisions.textEn:
1. Without prejudice to Article 156, the official or officer in charge of enforcing the order of precautionary detention shall provide the accused person with a copy of the decision along with a clear and precise written notice. If the accused does not know the Italian language, the notice shall be translated into a language he/she understands. The notice shall contain the following information:

b) his/her right to obtain information on the accusations raised;

provisions.comment: At the time of the arrest/temporary detention ("fermo").
provisions.textEn:
1. The police officials and officers who have arrested or placed under temporary detention ("fermo") the perpetrator or to whom the arrested person has been surrendered, shall immediately inform the Public Prosecutor of the place where the perpetrator has been arrested or stopped.

They shall provide the arrested or stopped person with a written notice, drafted clearly and precisely. If the arrested or temporarily detained person does not know the Italian language, the notice shall be translated into a language he/she understands. The notice shall contain the following information:

b) his/her right to obtain information on the accusations raised;

items.text: 3. Member States shall ensure that, at the latest on submission of the merits of the accusation to a court, detailed information is provided on the accusation, including the nature and legal classification of the criminal offence, as well as the nature of participation by the accused person.

provisions.comment: The lack of detailed information on the accusation is sanctioned with nullity of the decree for committal to trial (see Article 181, para. 3, of the Italian Criminal Procedure Code).
provisions.textEn:
1. The decree for committal to trial shall contain:

[...]

c) the clear and precise description of the criminal act, the aggravating circumstances and those that may result in the application of security measures, indicating the relevant Articles of law;

[...]

2. The decree shall be considered null if the accused is not identified in a certain way or if one of the requirements provided for in paragraph 1, letters c) and f), are missing or insufficient.

[...]

provisions.comment: The lack of detailed information on the accusation is sanctioned with nullity of the decree for direct summons for trial (see Article 181, para. 3, of the Italian Criminal Procedure Code).
provisions.textEn:
1. The decree for direct summons for trial shall contain:

[...]

c) the clear and precise description of the criminal act, the aggravating circumstances and those that may result in the application of security measures, indicating the relevant articles of law;

[...]

2. The decree shall be null if the accused is not identified appropriately or if one of the requirements provided for in letters c), d), e) and f) of paragraph 1 is missing or insufficient. 

[...]

items.text: 4. Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons are informed promptly of any changes in the information given in accordance with this Article where this is necessary to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

provisions.comment:
This Article regulates the changes in the accusation made by the Prosecutor if the criminal act, during trial, turns out to be different from the one charged to the accused.

The Constitutional Court intervened with numerous declarations of unconstitutionality of the present Article aimed at introducing the full right for the defendant to request a special proceeding (the summary trial, the application of punishment upon request or the suspension of proceedings pending probation) after the modification of the accusation (see judgements n. 265/1994; 333/2009; 273/2014; 206/2017; 14/2020). Nevertheless, neither the Constitutional Court nor the Criminal Procedure Code provide for the right of the accused to be informed of such prerogative.
provisions.textEn:
1. If, during the trial evidentiary hearing, it emerges that the criminal act differs from its description provided in the decree for committal to trial and does not fall within the competence of a higher court, the Public Prosecutor shall modify the accusation and bring it against the accused.

1 -bis. If, after the modification, it emerges that the offence should have been assigned to the cognisance of the collegial Tribunal, rather than to a single-judge Tribunal, the failure to comply with the provisions on the composition of the Tribunal shall be raised or objected, under penalty of expiry, either immediately after the new accusation is brought against the accused or, in the cases referred to in Articles 519, paragraph 2, and 520, paragraph 2, before carrying out any other action during the new hearing set under the aforementioned Articles.

1 -ter. If, after the modification, it emerges that the offence should have been treated in a preliminary hearing, but this did not occur, the failure to comply with the related provisions shall be objected, under penalty of expiry, within the time limit referred to in paragraph 1 -bis.

provisions.comment:
This Article regulates the changes in the accusation made by the Prosecutor if, during trial, a joined offence charged to the same accused or an aggravating circumstance emerges.

The Constitutional Court intervened with numerous declarations of unconstitutionality of the present Article aimed at introducing the full right for the defendant to request a special proceeding (the summary trial, the application of punishment upon request or the suspension of proceedings pending probation) after the modification of the accusation (see judgements n. 265/1994; 237/2012; 184/2014; 139/2015; 141/2018; 82/2019). Nevertheless, neither the Constitutional Court nor the Criminal Procedure Code provide for the right of the accused to be informed of such prerogative.
provisions.textEn:
1. If, during the trial evidentiary hearing, a joined offence under Article 12, paragraph 1, letter b) or an aggravating circumstance emerges, which is not mentioned in the decree for committal to trial, the Public Prosecutor shall bring an accusation concerning the offence or the circumstance against the accused, provided that the cognisance does not belong to a higher court.

1 -bis. The provisions of Article 516, paragraphs 1 -bis and 1 -ter, shall apply.

provisions.comment: This Article regulates the changes in the accusation made by the Prosecutor if, during trial, a new criminal act emerges. Contrary to Articles 516 and 517, pursuant to Article 518 such a modification is possible only with the authorisation of the President of the bench and with the consent of the accused.
provisions.textEn:
1. With the exception of the cases provided for in Article 517, the Public Prosecutor shall proceed following standard procedures, if a new criminal act emerges from the trial which is not mentioned in the decree for committal to trial and which is subject to prosecution of the Public Prosecutor‟s motion.

2. However, the President of the bench may authorise the accusation in the same hearing, if the Public Prosecutor requests so, if there is the consent of the accused present at the hearing and if this does not hinder the smooth development of proceedings.

provisions.comment:
The present Article lays down the right to information recognised to the accused in case of modifications in the accusation relating to the criminal act pursuant to Articles 516, 517 and 518, paragraph 2.

The Article has be declared unconstitutional by the Constitutional Court (judgments n. 241/1992 and 50/1995), as it did not extent the right to request the admission of new evidence to the Public Prosecutor and private parties other than the accused in case of modifications of the accusation pursuant to, respectively, Articles 516 and 517. Moreover, judgment n. 241/1992 declared the Article unconstitutional as it provided as criterion for the admission of new evidence the one of the "absolute necessity" (see Article 507 of the Italian Criminal Procedure Code), instead of the ordinary criteria set down by Articles 190 and 190-bis of the Italian Criminal Procedure Code.
provisions.textEn:
1. In the cases provided for in Articles 516, 517 and 518, paragraph 2, the President of the bench shall inform the accused of his/her right to request a period of time to prepare the defence, unless the accused has been charged with recidivism.

2. The President of the bench shall suspend the trial for a period of time equal to or longer than the time limit set for appearance under Article 429 (i.e. 20 days), and in any case for no more than forty days, if the accused requests so. In such case, the accused may request the admission of new evidence.

3. The President of the bench shall order the summoning of the victim, observing a time limit of at least five days.

provisions.comment: Procedure to be followed in the cases outlined under Articles 516 and 517 if the accused is not present at trial.
provisions.textEn:
1. If the Public Prosecutor intends to bring new accusations regarding the criminal acts or circumstances referred to in Articles 516 and 517 against the accused who is absent, he shall request the President of the bench that the new accusation be enclosed in the trial record and that the record be served on the accused in a summary form.

2. In such case, the President of the bench shall suspend the trial and set a new hearing, observing the time limits referred to in Article 519, paragraphs 2 and 3.

provisions.comment:
This Article enables the court to provide in the judgement for the correct legal qualification of the criminal act. Pursuant to the case-law implementing the ECtHR Drassich judgement, the accused is promptly informed of such modification of the accusation, at least when the new legal definition is detrimental for the defendant and when it was not sufficiently foreseable.

Instead, if according to the court the criminal act is different from the one charged to the accused, the case file is forwarded by the court to the Public Prosecutor.
provisions.textEn:
1. In the judgment, the court may provide a different legal definition of the criminal act from the one mentioned in the accusation, provided that the offence does not exceed the competence of the court and the cognisance of the single-judge Tribunal.

2. The court shall direct, by order, that the case file be forwarded to the Public Prosecutor if it ascertains that the criminal act is different from the one described in the decree for committal to trial or in the new accusation brought against the accused under Articles 516, 517 and 518, paragraph 2.

3. The court shall follow the same procedure if the Public Prosecutor has brought a new accusation other than those provided for in Articles 516, 517 and 518, paragraph 2.

provisions.comment: The lack of correlation between the accusation and the judgement is sanctioned with the nullity of the judgement.
provisions.textEn:
1. Failure to comply with the provisions referred to in this Chapter shall result in nullity.

2. The judgment of conviction delivered for a new criminal act, for a joined offence or an aggravating circumstance without observing the provisions of the previous Articles, shall be considered null, exclusively in the section dedicated to the new criminal act, the joined offence or the aggravating circumstance.

provisions.comment: The same discipline provided by Articles 516-518 in relation to the trial phase also applies to the preliminary hearing. At this stage, though, Article 519 relating to the information on the right to request a period of time to prepare the defence, is not applicable.
provisions.textEn:
1. If, during the hearing, it emerges that the criminal act differs from the description provided thereof in the accusation or it is a joined offence under Article 12, paragraph 1, letter b), or an aggravating circumstance emerges, the Public Prosecutor shall modify the accusation and bring it against the accused who is present. If the accused is not present, the modified accusation shall be brought against the lawyer who represents the accused.

2. If a new criminal act against the accused emerges, which is not listed in the request for committal to trial and is subject to prosecution of the Public Prosecutor‟s motion, the Preliminary Hearing Judge shall authorise its notification if the Public Prosecutor requests so and the accused gives his consent.

provisions.comment: The present Article regulates the declaration of the nullity by the appeals court for lack of correlation between the accusation and the first instance judgement.
provisions.textEn:
1. The appeal court, in the cases provided for in Article 522, shall declare the nullity of the appealed judgment, in whole or in part, and shall order that the case file be forwarded to the first-instance court, in the event of a conviction for a different criminal act or the application of an aggravating circumstance for which the law sets a type of penalty other than the standard one imposed for such offence or the application of an aggravating circumstance having special effect, provided that mitigating circumstances are not considered as prevailing or equivalent.

2. If mitigating circumstances are considered as prevailing or equivalent or aggravating circumstances other than those provided for in paragraph 1 are applied, the appeal court shall exclude the aggravating circumstances, perform a new comparison, if necessary, and establish a new penalty.

3. In case of conviction for a concurrent offence or a new criminal act, the appeal court shall declare the related section of the judgment null and eliminate the corresponding penalty, ordering that the new decision be forwarded to the Public Prosecutor for his decisions.

items.comment:
Under the Italian Criminal Procedure Code, the information relating to changes in the accusation is provided to the accused only in relation to modifications pertaining to the criminal act (see Article 519 below).

Nevertheless, following the Drassich v. Italy judgement of the European Court of Human Rights (2007), the Italian Supreme Court's case-law, in order to safeguard the effective exercise of the rights of the defence, recognises the right of the accused to be also informed of the modifications relating to the legal classification of the criminal offence (see Article 521 below).

items.heading: Article 7
items.subHeading: Right of access to the materials of the case
items.comment:
The Italian legislator did not consider it necessary to implement Article 7 in Legislative Decree no. 101/2014, that transposed Directive 2012/13 basically only with regard to the right to information.

However, pre-existing Italian legislation on the right of access to file could be partially considered in compliance with the Directive under this profile, while some critical profiles remaining with regard to the case of arrest and when it comes to applcable remedies.

items.text: 1. Where a person is arrested and detained at any stage of the criminal proceedings, Member States shall ensure that documents related to the specific case in the possession of the competent authorities which are essential to challenging effectively, in accordance with national law, the lawfulness of the arrest or detention, are made available to arrested persons or to their lawyers.

provisions.comment: Pre-trial detention
provisions.textEn: The orders referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 [ndr: orders applying pre-trial measures, including pre-trial detention] shall, after service or enforcement, be deposited at the Registry of the court which issued them, together with the request of the public prosecutor [to apply the pre-trial measure] and the documents submitted with it. Notice of the filing shall be served on the lawyer.

provisions.comment: Arrest and Stop; provision to be read jointly with Articles 388 and 391 c.p.p. and with Sez. U., no 36212 of 30/09/2010, G, Rv. 247939; Cass. pen. sez. VI, no. 9573, of 13/11/2019, Rv. 278623 - 01
provisions.textEn: Police officers and agents shall immediately inform of the arrest/the stop the lawyer appointed by the arrested person, or, if lacking the public defendant appointed by the public prosecutor pursuant to Article 97 c.p.p.

provisions.comment: Arrest and Stop; provision to be read jointly with Articles 386(2) and 391 c.p.p. and with Sez. U., no 36212 of 30/09/2010, G, Rv. 247939; Cass. pen. VI, no. 9573, of 10/11/2019, Rv. 278623 - 01
provisions.textEn:
1. The Public Prosecutor may proceed with the interrogation of the arrested or detained person, giving timely notice to the appointed lawyer or, failing that, to the public defender.


2. During the interrogation, having observed the forms provided for in Article 64, the Public Prosecutor shall inform the arrested or detained person of the fact for which the arrest or detention is being carried out; of the reasons which led to the measure; and of the elements against her/him, as well as, if it is not prejudicial to the investigation, of the sources from which such elements have been obtained.

provisions.comment: Arrest and Stop; provision to be read jointly with Articles 386(2) and 388 c.p.p. and with Sez. U., no 36212 of 30/09/2010, G, Rv. 247939; Cass. pen. sez. VI, no. 9573, of 13/11/2019, Rv. 278623 - 01
provisions.textEn:
1. The validation hearing shall take place in the council chamber with the necessary participation of the arrested or detained person's lawyer.


2. If the lawyer appointed by the arrested or detained has not been found or has not appeared, the judge shall proceed in accordance with Article 97(4). The judge verifies, also ex officio, that the arrested or detained person has been given the communication referred to in article 386(1), or that s/he has in any case been informed in accordance with paragraph 1-bis of the same article, and, if necessary, gives or completes the communication or information indicated therein.


3. The Public Prosecutor, if s/he appears, shall state the reasons for the arrest or detention and shall explain her/his requests concerning personal freedom. The judge then proceeds to question the arrested or detained person, unless s/he could not or refused to appear; in any case, the judge will hear her/his defence counsel.


4. When it appears that the arrest or detention has been lawfully carried out and the terms provided for in articles 386(3) and 390(1) have been observed, the judge shall validate the arrest or detention by order. The public prosecutor and the arrested or detained person may appeal against the order that decides on such validation.


[...]

provisions.comment: Access to the material of the case could be always requested to the proceeding authorities. The prosecutor has discretion in granting such access before the conclusion of the investigation, with the exception of the cases examined by Sez. U., no 36212 of 30/09/2010, G, Rv. 247939; Cass. pen. sez. VI, no. 9573, of 13/11/2019, Rv. 278623 - 01
provisions.textEn:
1. During the proceeding and after its settlement, any person having an interest therein may obtain the issuance at his/her own expense of copies, extracts or certificates of individual acts.


2. The request is dealt with by the public prosecutor's office or the judge who is proceeding at the time the request is presented or, after the conclusion of the proceedings, by the chairman of the panel or the judge who has issued the decision to dismiss or the sentence.

[...]

items.comment: The provision can be considered de facto implemented with regard to the detained person (subject to precautionary measures), cfr. Art. 293(3) CCP. On the other side, the provision is not implemented by statutory law with regard to the arrested or stopped person (fermo); the case-law of the Supreme Court, however, has recognized the right of access to file before the hearing to confirm the arrest, thus integrating the lacunas of the legal basis (Sez. U., no 36212 of 30/09/2010, G, Rv. 247939; Cass. pen. VI, no. 9573, of 13/11/2019, Rv. 278623 - 01)

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that access is granted at least to all material evidence in the possession of the competent authorities, whether for or against suspects or accused persons, to those persons or their lawyers in order to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings and to prepare the defence.

provisions.comment: Pre-trial detention
provisions.textEn: The orders referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 [ndr: orders applying pre-trial measures, including pre-trial detention] shall, after service or enforcement, be deposited at the Registry of the court which issued them, together with the request of the public prosecutor [to apply the pre-trial measure] and the documents submitted with it. Notice of the filing shall be served on the lawyer.

provisions.comment: Arrest or stop (fermo); the provision could be considered partially compliant with the Directive thanks to the case law of the Supreme Court, cf. Sez. U., no 36212 of 30/09/2010, G, Rv. 247939; Cass. pen. sez. VI, no. 9573, of 13/11/2019, Rv. 278623 - 01
provisions.textEn:
1. The Public Prosecutor may proceed with the interrogation of the arrested or detained person, giving timely notice to the appointed lawyer or, failing that, to the public defender.


2. During the interrogation, having observed the forms provided for in Article 64, the Public Prosecutor shall inform the arrested or detained person of the fact for which the arrest or detention is being carried out; of the reasons which led to the measure; and of the elements against her/him, as well as, if it is not prejudicial to the investigation, of the sources from which such elements have been obtained.

provisions.comment: At the end of the pre-trial investigation; the provision could be considered partially compliant with the Directive thanks to the case law of the Supreme Court, cf. Sez. U., no 36212 of 30/09/2010, G, Rv. 247939; Cass. pen. sez. VI, no. 9573, of 13/11/2019, Rv. 278623 - 01
provisions.textEn:
1. Before the expiry of the time limit provided for in paragraph 2 of article 405, even if extended, the Public Prosecutor, if s/he does not have to make a request for dismissal pursuant to articles 408 and 411, shall have the person under investigation and the defence counsel, as well as, when proceeding with the offences referred to in articles 572 and 612-bis of the Criminal Code, the defence counsel of the victim or, failing that, to the victim, notified of the conclusion of the preliminary investigations.


2. The notice shall contain a summary statement of the fact in respect of which the case is being prosecuted, the rules of law allegedly breached, the date and place of the fact, with the warning that the documents relating to the investigation carried out shall be filed with the Public Prosecutor's Office and that the suspect and her/his lawyer shall be entitled to inspect and extract a copy.


2a. If no action has been taken pursuant to article 268, paragraphs 4, 5 and 6, the notice shall also contain the warning that the suspect and her/his defence counsel have the right to examine by electronic means the acts relating to interceptions and listen to the recordings, or to take cognizance of the computer or telematic communication flows and that they have the right to extract copies of the recordings or flows indicated as relevant by the Public Prosecutor. The defence lawyer may, within twenty days, file the list of further recordings considered relevant and of which he requests a copy. The Public Prosecutor shall provide for the request by means of a reasoned decree. In the event of rejection of the request, or if there are objections to the indications relating to the registrations considered relevant, the defence lawyer may submit the request to the judge to proceed in the manner set out in article 268, paragraph 6.

items.comment: The provision can be considered partially implemented with regard to the detained person (subject to precautionary measures), cf. Art. 293(3) CCP and, thanks to the case-law of the Supreme Court (Sez. U., no 36212 of 30/09/2010, G, Rv. 247939; Cass. pen. VI, no. 9573, of 13/11/2019, Rv. 278623 - 01) with regard to the arrested or stopped person (fermo). However, the legislation and case-law refer exclusively to the elements on which the measure or request for arrest/fermo validation is grounded; no mention is instead done to potential elements in favour of the accused.

items.text: 3. Without prejudice to paragraph 1, access to the materials referred to in paragraph 2 shall be granted in due time to allow the effective exercise of the rights of the defence and at the latest upon submission of the merits of the accusation to the judgment of a court. Where further material evidence comes into the possession of the competent authorities, access shall be granted to it in due time to allow for it to be considered.

provisions.comment: At the end of the pre-trial investigation
provisions.textEn:
1. Before the expiry of the time limit provided for in paragraph 2 of article 405, even if extended, the Public Prosecutor, if s/he does not have to make a request for dismissal pursuant to articles 408 and 411, shall have the person under investigation and the defence counsel, as well as, when proceeding with the offences referred to in articles 572 and 612-bis of the Criminal Code, the defence counsel of the victim or, failing that, to the victim, notified of the conclusion of the preliminary investigations.


2. The notice shall contain a summary statement of the fact in respect of which the case is being prosecuted, the rules of law allegedly breached, the date and place of the fact, with the warning that the documents relating to the investigation carried out shall be filed with the Public Prosecutor's Office and that the suspect and her/his lawyer shall be entitled to inspect and extract a copy.


2a. If no action has been taken pursuant to article 268, paragraphs 4, 5 and 6, the notice shall also contain the warning that the suspect and her/his defence counsel have the right to examine by electronic means the acts relating to interceptions and listen to the recordings, or to take cognizance of the computer or telematic communication flows and that they have the right to extract copies of the recordings or flows indicated as relevant by the Public Prosecutor. The defence lawyer may, within twenty days, file the list of further recordings considered relevant and of which he requests a copy. The Public Prosecutor shall provide for the request by means of a reasoned decree. In the event of rejection of the request, or if there are objections to the indications relating to the registrations considered relevant, the defence lawyer may submit the request to the judge to proceed in the manner set out in article 268, paragraph 6.

items.text: 4. By way of derogation from paragraphs 2 and 3, provided that this does not prejudice the right to a fair trial, access to certain materials may be refused if such access may lead to a serious threat to the life or the fundamental rights of another person or if such refusal is strictly necessary to safeguard an important public interest, such as in cases where access could prejudice an ongoing investigation or seriously harm the national security of the Member State in which the criminal proceedings are instituted. Member States shall ensure that, in accordance with procedures in national law, a decision to refuse access to certain materials in accordance with this paragraph is taken by a judicial authority or is at least subject to judicial review.

provisions.comment:
The decision not to disclose the sources from which elements against the accused have been obtained is taken by the Public prosecutor, which in the Italian legal system enjoys the same status of court judges. However, some ECtHR case law and legal scholars highlighted that the prosecutor cannot be really considered as a impartial subject within criminal proceedings, even during pre-trial investigations (cfr., e.g., ECtHR, Brazzi vs Italy, App. no. 57278/11 of 27.09.2018; Lasagni, G. (2018). Tackling phone searches in Italy and the United States: Proposals for a technological rethinking of procedural rights and freedoms. New Journal of European Criminal Law, 9(3), 386–401, https://doi.org/10.1177/2032284418798053).

In this sense, the lack of specific judicial review against decisions refusing to granting access to certain material - differently from what established by Article 415bis (2bis) with regard to interception, at the end of the pre-trial investigation - can be seen as problematic in terms of compliance with the Directive.
provisions.textEn:
1. The Public Prosecutor may proceed with the interrogation of the arrested or detained person, giving timely notice to the appointed lawyer or, failing that, to the public defender.


2. During the interrogation, having observed the forms provided for in Article 64, the Public Prosecutor shall inform the arrested or detained person of the fact for which the arrest or detention is being carried out; of the reasons which led to the measure; and of the elements against her/him, as well as, if it is not prejudicial to the investigation, of the sources from which such elements have been obtained.

1. Acts of investigation carried out by the public prosecutor and the police, requests by the public prosecutor for authorisation to carry out investigative acts and the acts of the judge ruling on such requests shall be covered by secrecy until the defendant has knowledge of them and, in any case, not beyond the closure of the preliminary investigations

2. When it is necessary for the continuation of the investigations, the Public Prosecutor may, by way of derogation from Article 114, allow, by reasoned decree, the publication of individual acts or parts thereof. In this case, the published acts shall be filed with the secretariat of the public prosecutor's office.

3. Even when the acts are no longer covered by secrecy pursuant to subsection 1, the Public Prosecutor, if necessary for the continuation of the investigation, may, by means of a motivated decree, order

(a) the obligation of secrecy for individual acts, when the defendant consents or when knowledge of the act may hinder investigations concerning other persons;

(b) the prohibition to publish the contents of individual acts or specific information concerning certain operations.

items.comment: Partially transposed. In general terms, the only exception allowed in the Italian legal order concerns the potential prejudice for ongoing investigation; the term is however so broad that it could well encompass also the other exceptions listed in paragraph 4.

items.text: 5. Access, as referred to in this Article, shall be provided free of charge.

provisions.comment: The possibility to charge fees in exchange for the release of copies seems in compliance with Recital (34) of the Directive: Access to the materials of the case, as provided for by this Directive, should be provided free of charge, without prejudice to provisions of national law providing for fees to be paid for documents to be copied from the case file or for sending materials to the persons concerned or to their lawyer.

1. During the proceedings and after they have been settled, anyone interested in them may obtain copies, extracts or certificates of individual documents at their own expense.


2. The request shall be dealt with by the public prosecutor's office or the judge proceeding at the time the request is made or, after the proceedings have been concluded, by the chairperson of the panel or the judge who issued the order to close the case or the judgment.

items.heading: Article 8

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that when information is provided to suspects or accused persons in accordance with Articles 3 to 6 this is noted using the recording procedure specified in the law of the Member State concerned.

provisions.comment: Record relating to the information given by the police at the time of the enforcement of a precautionary detention order.
provisions.textEn: The official or officer in charge of enforcing the order shall immediately inform the retained lawyer or the lawyer appointed by the court in accordance with Article 97 and shall draft a record of all the activities carried out, including the delivery of the written notice referred to in paragraph 1 or the information provided orally in accordance with paragraph 1 -bis. The record shall be immediately forwarded to the court who has issued the order and to the Public Prosecutor.

provisions.comment: Record relating to the information given by the police at the time of the arrest/temporary detention ("fermo").
provisions.textEn: If the case envisaged in Article 389, paragraph 2, does not occur, police officials and officers shall place the arrested or temporarily detained person ("fermato") at the disposal of the Public Prosecutor as soon as possible and, in any case, within twenty-four hours of the arrest or start of temporary detention. Within the same time limit they shall forward the relevant record, also electronically, unless the Public Prosecutor authorises a longer time limit. The record shall contain the possible appointment of a retained lawyer, the specification of the day, time and place in which the person was arrested or placed under temporary detention and a list of the reasons thereof, as well as the specification that the arrested or temporarily detained person was provided with the written notice or orally informed according to paragraph 1 -bis.

provisions.comment: General recording methods.
provisions.textEn:
1. Acts shall be reported in records.

2. Records shall be drafted, fully or in summary form, by means of either a stenotype machine, any other mechanical tool or, in case these tools are not available, handwritten notes.

3. If records are drafted in summary form, audio recordings shall also be made.

4. If the recording methods referred to in paragraphs 2 and 3 are considered insufficient, an audiovisual recording may be added, if absolutely essential. Audiovisual recordings of the statements made by a victim with specific protection needs may be made in any case, even when they are not absolutely essential.

provisions.comment: Documentation of the questioning of the detained person.
provisions.textEn: 1. Any questioning conducted outside the hearing of a person who is detained for any reason is to be documented fully, under penalty of exclusion, by means of audio or audiovisual recording. If recording tools or technical personnel are unavailable, reports by either experts or technical consultants shall be required. The questioning shall also be recorded in summary form. The transcription of the recording shall be ordered only upon request of the parties.

items.comment:
Specific framework relating to the recording procedure is explicitly implemented only in relation to the information given to the suspect or accused persons deprived of liberty by the police (see art. 293 par. 1 ter and 386 par. 3 Criminla Procedure Code below). Such recording is documentary according to Italian law (see Article 134 of the Italian Criminal Procedure Code).

As for the information given during questioning of the suspect deprived of liberty (see articles 64 and 294 par. 1 bis Criminal Procedure Code), in this case the questioning is also video or audio recorded (see art. 141 bis of the Criminal Procedure Code). Otherwise, if the suspect is not deprived of liberty or during court hearings (see e.g. art. 391 par. 3 Criminal Procedure Code), the recording of the questioning is only documentary pursuant to art. 134 Criminal Procedure Code.

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons or their lawyers have the right to challenge, in accordance with procedures in national law, the possible failure or refusal of the competent authorities to provide information in accordance with this Directive.

The request shall be considered null if it is not preceded by the warnings provided for in Article 415-bis, as well as by the summons to appear for questioning according to Article 375, paragraph 3, if the suspect has requested the questioning within the time limit referred to in Article 415-bis, paragraph 3.

items.comment:
PARTIAL IMPLEMENTATION

In general terms, if the accused is not provided for with the information rights throught the Letter of Rights, s/he can still be informed by the competent judge, who controls the legality of measures affecting personal freedom (see Articles 294bis and 391(2) c.p.p.). When even this opportunity fails, no specific remedy has been introduced in the Italian legal framework to address violations of the rights included in the Directive.

However, to some extent, the previously existing legislation already provided for some remedy in case of certain violations of the rights contained in this Directive. In this regard, it could be considered that Article 8(2) is partially and indirectly implemented in Italy.


Specifically, remedies were already recognized in the following cases, concerning the right to information:


* in connection with the right to access to a lawyer (Articles 369, 369bis, 386(1)(a), 293(1)(a), 386(1)(a) c.p.p.): Violations of this information right are sanctioned with nullity ex Article 178 (1), let. c) c.p.p. (nullità intermedia), which may be raised by the parties and ex officio within specific time limits that follow the different phases of criminal proceedings (not after the decision of first instance for violations occurred before the trial hearing; for those occurred at trial, not after the decision of the following instance). In case of violation of Article 293 c.p.p., such nullity may also be invoked through the specific appeal remedies established against pre-trial measures (Article 309 ff c.p.p.).


* in connection with the right to be informed of the accusation ex Articles 293, 386 c.p.p.: Violations of this information rights are sanctioned with nullity ex Article 178 (1), let. c) c.p.p. (nullità intermedia), which may be raised also ex officio within specific time limits that follow the different phases of criminal proceedings (not after the decision of first instance for violations occurred before the trial hearing; for those occurred during the trial, not after the decision of the following instance). In case of violation of Article 293 c.p.p., such nullity may also be invoked through the specific appeal remedies established against pre-trial measures (Article 309 ff c.p.p.).

According to the jurisprudence, however the nullity related to Art. 386 c.p.p. is considered to be able to afftect only the arrest, and not the validity of the following proceeding (cfr. Cass., Sez. II, no. 6013 of 30/01/2018, Rv. 272676-01).


* in connection with the right to be informed of the accusation ex Article 415bis(2) c.p.p.: if the warnings of Article 415bis are missing, the request to proceed to trial (Article 416 c.p.p.) is sanctioned by nullity.


* in connection with the right to be informed of any changes in the information given, and specifically of potential changes in the accusation, ex Articles 423, 516, 517, 518, 520, 521, 604 c.p.p.: Violations of these information rights are sanctioned with the nullity of the decision in accordance with Article 522 c.p.p.


* in connection with the right to remain silent (Articles 63 and 64 c.p.p.): Violations of this information right are sanctioned by exclusionary rule, that is, statements obtained without the previous warning cannot be used as evidence, unless they are in favour of the suspect (cf. Cass. Sez. Un., 13 December 1996, RV 206846)


*in connection with the right to be informed of: the right to interpretation/translation; the right to communicate with third-parties and consular authorities; the right to medical assistance; the maximum number of hours or days suspects or accused persons may be deprived of liberty before being brought before a judicial authority; the remedies applicable. Violations of these information rights are sanctioned with nullity ex Article 178 (1), let. c) c.p.p. (nullità intermedia), which may be raised in accordance to the deadlines illustrated above.


On the contrary, no remedy is provided for in the following cases, where, therefore, the Italian legal framework cannot be considered in compliance (or in full compliance) with the Directive:


* in connection with the right to be informed of the accusation ex Article 335 c.p.p. (for the violation of which only disciplinary sanctions might be applicable, cf. S. Ciampi, Diritto all'informazione nei procedimenti penali: il recepimento low profile della Direttiva 2012/13/UE da parte del d. lsg. 1° luglio 2014 n. 101. Letter of Rights e Full Disclosure nel procedimento penale italiano, in Dir. pen. cont., 24 September 2014, p. 9; contra P. Gualtieri, Registro delle notizie di reato: i problemi del dopo riforma. Il punto di vista di un avvocato, in Dir. pen. proc., 1996, p. 498)


Breaches of the right of access to file

Remedies to violation of the right to access to the material of the case find their legal bases almost exclusively in the case-law.

In particular, according to the Supreme Court, the refusal of the right to access, to the extent the latter is recognized during the investigation, causes a nullity (nullità generale a regime intermedio) of the subsequent interview of the accused and of the act that validates his/her arrest. Such nullity shall, in any case, be raised during the hearing scheduled to validate the arrest ex Art 182, c. 2 cpp (and not to a later stage of the proceeding), cfr. Sez. U., no 36212 of 30/09/2010, G, Rv. 247939.

A (at least partial) statutory legal basis may instead be found with regard to the right of access to file after the conclusion of the investigations. Indeed, violations of the requirements listed by Art 415 bis cpp causes the nullity of the subsequent request to proceed to trial (Art 416 cpp). Nonetheless, besides for potential disciplinary liability of the Prosecutor, no specific provision is established to remedy to the (unlikely) situation where the defendant is prevented from actually accessing to the file.


Breaches occured within EAW proceedings:

This specific regulation is provided for by Art. 12(3) Law 69/2005, which under several profiles does not provide fully satisfactory remedies in case of violations of the rights contained in the Directive.


*Art. 12(3) establishes a sanction of nullity (nullità relativa) in case the arrest report does not refer to the fullfillment of the informative obligations provided for by Art. 12(1) of the same Law:

  • information, in a language that the person understands, of the warrant issued and of its content;
  • information in a written form, drawn up in a clear and precise manner, of the possibility to consent to his/her surrender to the issuing judicial authority
  • information in a written form, drawn up in a clear and precise manner, of right to appoint a lawyer (in the executing State);
  • information in a written form, drawn up in a clear and precise manner, of right to be assisted by an interpreter.

The level of protection, in this case, is therefore not equal to that conferred in national proceedings, where the nullity is triggered by the fact that the information is not given to the defendant (and not by the fact that the fullfillment of the informative obligations is not mentioned in the arrest report).


*On the other side, the information on the right to appoint a lawyer in the issuing State (provided for by Art. 9(5bis) Law 69/2005, recalled by Art. 12(1bis) Law 69/2005) is excluded from such nullity. With regard to this provision, therefore, no specific remedy is currently available at the legislative level. The case-law explicitly considered that this information can also be given to the defendant in a subsequent moment, that is by the judge while confirming the arrest, ex Art. 391 and 294 c.p.p. (cfr. Cass. Sez. VI, no. 52013 of 16/10/2018, Rv. 274611-01).


*Lastly (as highlighted also by Art. 5 of this Directive) some information rights are not recognized to the defendant in case of EAW (right to silent, right to be informed of the changes in the accusation). In this case, therefore, also no specific remedy exists in case of their violation. Although the asimmetry between national and EAW proceedings seems to have been sustained by the Court of Justice (Spetsializirana prokuratura, case C-649/19 of 28 January 2021, ECLI:EU:C:2021:75), the difference of treatment still appears critical in the perspective of an effective protection of defence rights.

The sole purpose of this model is to assist national authorities in drawing up their Letter of Rights at national level. Member States are not bound to use this model. When preparing their Letter of Rights, Member States may amend this model in order to align it with their national rules and add further useful information. The Member State’s Letter of Rights must be given upon arrest or detention. This however does not prevent Member States from providing suspects or accused persons with written information in other situations during criminal proceedings.


A. ASSISTANCE OF A LAWYER/ENTITLEMENT TO LEGAL AID


You have the right to speak confidentially to a lawyer. A lawyer is independent from the police. Ask the police if you need help to get in contact with a lawyer, the police shall help you. In certain cases the assistance may be free of charge. Ask the police for more information.


B. INFORMATION ABOUT THE ACCUSATION


You have the right to know why you have been arrested or detained and what you are suspected or accused of having done.


C. INTERPRETATION AND TRANSLATION


If you do not speak or understand the language spoken by the police or other competent authorities, you have the right to be assisted by an interpreter, free of charge. The interpreter may help you to talk to your lawyer and must keep the content of that communication confidential. You have the right to translation of at least the relevant passages of essential documents, including any order by a judge allowing your arrest or keeping you in custody, any charge or indictment and any judgment. You may in some circumstances be provided with an oral translation or summary.


D. RIGHT TO REMAIN SILENT


While questioned by the police or other competent authorities, you do not have to answer questions about the alleged offence. Your lawyer can help you to decide on that.


E. ACCESS TO DOCUMENTS


When you are arrested and detained, you (or your lawyer) have the right to access essential documents you need to challenge the arrest or detention. If your case goes to court, you (or your lawyer) have the right to access the material evidence for or against you.


F. INFORMING SOMEONE ELSE ABOUT YOUR ARREST OR DETENTION/INFORMING YOUR CONSULATE OR EMBASSY


When you are arrested or detained, you should tell the police if you want someone to be informed of your detention, for example a family member or your employer. In certain cases the right to inform another person of your detention may be temporarily restricted. In such cases the police will inform you of this.


If you are a foreigner, tell the police if you want your consular authority or embassy to be informed of your detention. Please also tell the police if you want to contact an official of your consular authority or embassy.


G. URGENT MEDICAL ASSISTANCE


When you are arrested or detained, you have the right to urgent medical assistance. Please let the police know if you are in need of such assistance.


H. PERIOD OF DEPRIVATION OF LIBERTY


After your arrest you may be deprived of liberty or detained for a maximum period of … [fill in applicable number of hours/days]. At the end of that period you must either be released or be heard by a judge who will decide on your further detention. Ask your lawyer or the judge for information about the possibility to challenge your arrest, to review the detention or to ask for provisional release.
items.heading: ANNEX I
items.comment:
The Italian Ministry of the Interior on 11 August 2014 drew up a model Letter of Rights in Italian, with translations into English, French, Spanish, German and Chinese. It can be found at the following link: https://dati.asaps.it/leggi/circolari/ministero_interno/2014-INTERNI_n_22571_del_11082014.pdf.

A model including the Arabic language would be desirable.

As it can be seen, the Italian model, contrary to Annex I, is not detailed as for the meaning of the rights listed. Therefore, the accessibility of the content of the Letter of Rights might be jeopardised.

A. INFORMATION ABOUT THE EUROPEAN ARREST WARRANT


You have the right to be informed about the content of the European Arrest Warrant on the basis of which you have been arrested.


B. ASSISTANCE OF A LAWYER


You have the right to speak confidentially to a lawyer. A lawyer is independent from the police. Ask the police if you need help to get in contact with a lawyer, the police shall help you. In certain cases the assistance may be free of charge. Ask the police for more information.


C. INTERPRETATION AND TRANSLATION


If you do not speak or understand the language spoken by the police or other competent authorities, you have the right to be assisted by an interpreter, free of charge. The interpreter may help you to talk to your lawyer and must keep the content of that communication confidential. You have the right to a translation of the European Arrest Warrant in a language you understand. You may in some circumstances be provided with an oral translation or summary.


D. POSSIBILITY TO CONSENT


You may consent or not consent to being surrendered to the State seeking you. Your consent would speed up the proceedings. [Possible addition of certain Member States: It may be difficult or even impossible to change this decision at a later stage.] Ask the authorities or your lawyer for more information.


E. HEARING


If you do not consent to your surrender, you have the right to be heard by a judicial authority.
